description: Pure, tested chart-data helpers for the series-flow visualization (Issue #24). Build dependency-free functions that turn a Series (and, for predictable seasons, the pure predict()) into the data arrays the SVG charts and their tabular alternatives render from. The win-probability trend MUST reuse the per-game truncation approach already implemented in @mlb/shared backtest.ts sampleSeries (slice to first k games, recompute high/low wins, call predict) rather than duplicating truncation logic, keeping predict() the single source of truth. This is foundational and independent of the React rendering in FEAT-002/003.
steps: Decide placement: create frontend/src/seriesCharts.ts (frontend-only pure helpers; the charts are frontend concerns and the file imports @mlb/shared types + predict + the shared truncation). Export the data types and functions below. Keep it dependency-free (no React), mirroring the style of frontend/src/gameTime.ts / upcomingGames.ts.

Implement seriesScoreDiffs(series: Series): per-game array of { gameNumber, awayTeamId, homeTeamId, awayScore, homeScore, winnerTeamId (via isWinner, null if neither), diff (|awayScore-homeScore|, 0 when a score is null) }. Sort games by seriesGameNumber ascending. Handle null scores gracefully (diff 0, winnerTeamId null).

Implement cumulativeWinTrend(series: Series): running series-win totals after each game as an array of { gameNumber, highWins, lowWins } where highWins/lowWins count isWinner among games 1..k for series.high.teamId / series.low.teamId (reuse the same counting semantics as backtest.ts countWins; do not trust stored final win counts). First entry is after game 1.

Implement winProbTrend(series, bracket, accuracy): per-game favorite win probability using the SAME truncation as backtest.ts sampleSeries. Prefer to EXPORT a reusable per-game helper from shared/src/backtest.ts (e.g. export the existing sampleSeries OR add a thin exported seriesProbTrend(series, bracket, accuracy) that returns [{ gameNumber, favoriteTeamId, favoriteWinProbability }] built from the first-k-games truncation + predict) and have winProbTrend delegate to it, so truncation lives in ONE place. If exporting from shared, keep backtest's existing behavior/tests unchanged (additive export only). winProbTrend returns [] for a series with no games.

Add exact-number unit tests in frontend/src/seriesCharts.test.ts (and, if shared helper added, extend shared/src/backtest.test.ts additively). Use fixtures including: (a) a SWEEP series (e.g. 2-0 or 4-0, lopsided large diffs) and (b) a tight/close series (1-run games, goes the distance) — assert the EXACT diff values, exact cumulative win arrays, and exact winProbTrend probabilities (pin the numbers predict() produces at accuracy 0.5). Cover a null-score / in-progress game edge case.
Run the shared + frontend unit tests to confirm the new helpers pass and the existing backtest tests are unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: frontend/src/seriesCharts.ts exports seriesScoreDiffs, cumulativeWinTrend, winProbTrend (plus their result types) and is React-free / pure.

winProbTrend reuses backtest.ts truncation (via an exported shared helper or by calling the existing per-game logic) and does NOT duplicate the slice/recompute-wins logic; predict() remains the only probability source.
frontend/src/seriesCharts.test.ts asserts exact numbers for a lopsided sweep series, a close full-length series, and a null-score edge case; all pass under npm test.
Existing shared backtest tests still pass unchanged (any shared export is additive).
findings: Implemented the pure chart-data helpers in frontend/src/seriesCharts.ts (React-free, mirrors gameTime.ts style): seriesScoreDiffs, cumulativeWinTrend, winProbTrend, each with exported result types (SeriesScoreDiff, CumulativeWinPoint, WinProbPoint). ADDED an additive shared export seriesProbTrend(series, bracket, accuracy) -> SeriesProbTrendPoint[] in shared/src/backtest.ts: it now OWNS the per-game truncation (sort by seriesGameNumber, slice first k games, recompute high/low wins via countWins, call predict). Refactored the private sampleSeries to DELEGATE to seriesProbTrend and layer only eventual-winner scoring on top, so the truncation lives in exactly one place and predict() stays the single probability source. winProbTrend simply delegates to seriesProbTrend; it does NOT require a final series (truncates whatever games exist) and returns [] for a games-less series. seriesScoreDiffs: winner via isWinner (null if neither), diff = |away-home| or 0 when a score is null. cumulativeWinTrend: recomputes isWinner counts for high/low per game 1..k (does not trust stored final win counts). Tests added in frontend/src/seriesCharts.test.ts (15 tests) with EXACT pinned numbers at accuracy 0.5: SWEEP (bestOf5, low=119 sweeps high=147 3-0, diffs [9,8,7], winProb [0.6928,0.7839,0.8333]); CLOSE (bestOf7, high=119 beats low=147 4-3 in 1-run games, all diffs 1, winners [119,147,147,119,147,119,119], winProb [0.697,0.5149,0.5917,0.5098,0.5649,0.5073,0.5631]); IN-PROGRESS/null-score (game1 121 wins, game2 null scores -> diff 0 / winnerTeamId null / not counted as win, winProb [0.697,0.697]); plus games-less [] cases. Extended shared/src/backtest.test.ts additively with a 'seriesProbTrend' describe block (empty-series [], seed-bracket consistency/clamp checks, in-progress truncation pinned to 0.697); existing backtest tests unchanged. Verification all green: npm test -w @mlb/shared (37 tests), npm test -w @mlb/frontend (178 tests), npm run build (shared->backend->frontend->infra). Did add a shared export (seriesProbTrend); it is additive and backtest behavior/tests are unchanged.
